1_jekyll.body: one man only, Dr Henry Jekyll, full figure head to feet, standing alone on a foggy gaslit London street at night. A large, broad, heavy-set, handsome man of fifty, tall and of fine build, with a full, broad, smooth face and large, firm, white and comely hands. Thick iron-grey hair, silver-grey at the temples and sides, brushed back from a high forehead; smooth-faced and clean-shaven; a tall black silk top hat. Dressed in a good dark frock coat and waistcoat, a respectable professional man, calm and composed.

2_hyde.body: one man only, Mr Edward Hyde, full figure head to feet, standing alone on a foggy gaslit London street at night. A small, slight, sinister young man of about twenty-five, short and narrow-shouldered, pale, his thin upper lip curled in a cold sneer, a displeasing smile, with lean, corded, knuckly hands of a dusky pallor. Coarse, unkempt black hair; thick, bushy black mutton-chop side-whiskers down both cheeks to the jaw; a soft black felt wideawake hat with a low flat crown and a wide floppy brim. In a dark coat that fits him badly, hunched and coiled.

3_utterson.body: one man only, Mr Gabriel John Utterson the lawyer, full figure head to feet, standing alone on a foggy gaslit London street at night. A lean, long, bony, dry man of about forty, narrow-chested, with a long, gaunt, rugged face that is never lighted by a smile. Lank, sandy-blond dust-fair hair falling to his collar, thin at the crown; clean-shaven; a black bowler hat. In a sober black suit with a high collar under a long greatcoat.

4_door.body: an empty narrow London back street at night, seen from the cobbles: a sinister two-storey block of building thrusts its gable forward onto the street; the upper storey is a flat blank wall of stained, discoloured plaster; below it one blistered, discoloured, paint-stained door with neither bell nor knocker, set in a shallow recess at the top of two worn stone steps; wet black cobbles, one gas lamp glowing through thick yellow fog, deep shadow, no people, no figures.

2_trampling.body: chapter 1, three o'clock on a black winter morning at a deserted London street corner under one gas lamp. Mr Edward Hyde, a small, slight, sinister young man of about twenty-five, pale, with a cold sneer, coarse black hair and thick bushy black mutton-chop side-whiskers, in a soft black felt wideawake hat with a low flat crown and a wide floppy brim and a badly fitting dark coat, strides heavily forward and does not stop; a little girl of nine in a plain grey pinafore and a knitted bonnet, fair hair in two plaits, has fallen on the cobbles at his feet and looks up at him, frightened. A moment of cold menace: his shadow falls over her, his face lit from below by the gas lamp. Fog, black empty street, shuttered shopfronts, deep shadow. Two figures only.

4_carew.body: chapter 4, the Carew murder: a narrow London lane at night drowned in thick brown fog under a full moon. Mr Edward Hyde, a small, slight young man in a soft black felt wideawake hat with a low flat crown and a wide floppy brim and a badly fitting coat, black side-whiskers, seen almost in silhouette against the fog-glow of a gas lamp, raises a heavy straight walking cane high above his head with both hands, coiled to strike. In front of him, half turned away, a tall aged gentleman with long silky white hair and a short white beard, in a dark coat, lifts a hand. No blood, no gore; a frozen moment of menace. Wet cobbles, black railings, a moonlit fog bank. Two figures only.
